messages.subject: Significance stats from STAR model
messages.body_plain:
Dear Matthieu

I am a graduate student and a beginner in R. I would like to estimate a STAR model and came across the tsDyn package. For the STAR function, is there a way to view the standard error, t-statistic and corresponding p-value of the estimated coefficients? The summary command only displays the coefficients themselves. I might be missing something blatantly obvious, so please forgive the ignorance.

Regards,
Yudhvir Seetharam

messages.subject: Re: Significance stats from STAR model
messages.body_plain:
Dear Yudhvir

Sorry for the late reply.

Unfortunately, for the star() function, there is currently no summary() function giving the t-stats/p-val. However, the lstar() function hsa a summary(9 funciton that will give you all the required infromations.

Best

Matthieu

messages.subject: Re: question about tsDyn
messages.body_plain:
Dear Bo

Sorry for the late reply. You are right, there is currently no possibility to add an intercept in the cointegration for TVECM(). And yes, as long as the user is giving a pre-specified value, a one dimensional grid would not be too complicated to add. But unfortunately, that will remain on the wish list, and as far as I can see, not implemented anytime soon :-(

Best

Matthieu

Le 19. 11. 14 12:26, Bo Chen a écrit :
> Hi Matthie,
>
> I have a question about the TVECM command in the tsDyn package. The cointegration vector (beta) can be either determined by a double grid search together with threshold parameter (gamma) or can be supplied explicitly. Either way, there is no intercept in the cointegration space and this is a fairly strong specification. My question is: is it possible to include an intercept in the cointegration space and the cointegration vectors (both the slope and intercept) can be supplied by the researcher so that a single grid search over gamma is all needed to estimate the model?
>
> Thank you.
>
